clue.text: Fabric conditioner more frequently used by son

parts.note: more frequently means oftener, the comparative of often

explanation.surface: A laundry product that a son reaches for more often than anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A softener is a laundry product that makes washed cloth feel smoother.

clue.text: Glide, say, round tree

indicators.note: round means the word for say is wrapped around the tree

parts.note: taken as written
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: An instruction to float, for instance, around a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to move with a smooth, swaying walk.

clue.text: Quick deal perhaps in northern port

parts.note: fleet means swift, quick
deal is a kind of pine timber, so an example of wood

explanation.surface: A speedy business transaction, maybe, in a harbour in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is not a transaction here but softwood timber. Fleetwood is a fishing port in Lancashire, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleetwood is a harbour town on the Lancashire coast of northern England.

clue.text: Ruler taking measure against the media

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measure
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: A monarch takes action against the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female sovereign governing an empire.

clue.text: Artist born in King Street

indicators.note: in means the born letter sits inside King plus Street

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, used here for royal ruler in general
N, from nee, is an abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: A painter was born on King Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Max Ernst was a German Surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a leading Surrealist painter and sculptor.

clue.text: Sleepy head?

parts.note: read as someone who dozes off, and also as old slang for the head itself

explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls the head a napper, and someone taking a nap is likewise one, so a drowsy noggin fits both ways.

clue.text: A youngster appeared finally in pantomime

parts.note: a lad is a young boy

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of appeared

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child made a stage appearance in a festive show.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show; Aladdin is a classic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Aladdin is one of the best-known British Christmas stage shows for families.

clue.text: Secretary has German messaging device

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: An office assistant owns a German-made gadget for messages.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is a small radio gadget that beeps to alert its owner to a call.

clue.text: Renovated shop with Monday's soluti red exterior

indicators.note: exterior means red forms the outside, with shop inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: A refurbished shop now has a red frontage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restored has been repaired and brought back to its former condition.

clue.text: Gets lots of paper on N R account

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone buys reams of stationery on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is an old paper measure of 24 or 25 sheets. In a down clue, 'on' means the second piece sits below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to come to possess it.

clue.text: Such reforms as are introduced by a new broom?

definitions.text: Such reforms as are introduced by a new broom?

parts.words: Such reforms as are introduced by a new broom?
parts.note: a new broom is a newly appointed boss who overhauls everything; the broom also literally brushes the floor

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a new broom sweeps clean' describes a fresh manager making radical reforms; the broom image makes the reforms literally done with a brush.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide-ranging reforms are far-reaching alterations, and a broom literally works by brushing in strokes.

clue.text: Some characters in parties tend to be most cultured

indicators.note: Some characters in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people at parties like to show off how refined they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty means having pretensions to culture, and the superlative form is the most so.

clue.text: Experience problem with one drug

indicators.note: a problem leaves things in disorder, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has trouble with a single medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' signals rearranging ONE and DRUG together.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience something unpleasant is to go through or suffer it.

clue.text: Think carefully about resistance by Conservative team

parts.note: a side is a sports team
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A Tory squad weighs up how much opposition it faces.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate on something is to give it thought before deciding.

clue.text: Despondent Irish players?

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland, so Irish suggests it
the cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: A gloomy troupe of actors from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means low in spirits, dejected.

clue.text: Husband occupies pleasant, comfortable position

indicators.note: occupies means the husband's letter takes up a place inside the other word

parts.note: pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: A married man settles into an agreeable, cosy spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or place that suits someone snugly, a cosy slot.

clue.text: Ancestor suspiciously D keeping posh W mistress

indicators.note: keeping means the jumbled letters hold the posh letter inside
suspiciously suggests something fishy, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: An ancestor shiftily keeps an upper-class lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspiciously' rearranges ANCESTOR into COURTESAN's other letters, and 'keeping' holds U (upper-class) inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan is a kept woman, the paid lover of rich men.

clue.text: Established to contain M freight, but one moves H G N at a snail's pace

definitions.text: one moves H G N at a snail's pace

indicators.note: to contain means established's abbreviation holds the freight inside

parts.note: cargo is freight

explanation.surface: A firm carries goods, but slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: an escargot is a snail, so it moves at a snail's pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French word for an edible snail, which crawls slowly.

clue.text: Former Egyptian president not happy with African tribal leaders

parts.note: not happy means sad

indicators.note: leaders points to the opening letters of the words African and tribal

explanation.surface: A one-time Egyptian leader is unhappy with chiefs from across Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Anwar Sadat was president of Egypt from 1970 to 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: Anwar Sadat led Egypt as head of state until his assassination in 1981.

clue.text: Several workers, B occupants of rented property

parts.note: ten stands for an unspecified several
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: A group of employees living in a rented home.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants are those who rent and live in a property owned by a landlord.

clue.text: Exhausted, having dealt with the dirty dishes

definitions.meaning: spent, finished, at the end of one's career

definitions.text: having dealt with the dirty dishes
definitions.meaning: having cleaned the plates after a meal

explanation.definitionFit: Washed-up is idiom for finished or spent, and literally describes someone who has done the dishes.

clue.text: Was Socialist leader left outside?

indicators.note: outside means left goes around the socialist's leading letter

parts.note: left means exited, went out

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of Socialist

explanation.surface: Asks whether a left-wing chief was shut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To have existed is to have been, the past of being.

clue.text: Look good and unusually clean

indicators.note: unusually means the letters appear in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: Something appears fine and remarkably tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a quick look.

clue.text: A fellow receives large bill for handbook

indicators.note: receives means the large letter goes inside A plus fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a man
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A man is handed a hefty invoice for a manual.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual reference book of facts and tables, a kind of guide.

clue.text: Mother runs after friend

indicators.note: after means runs is placed behind friend

parts.note: a mate is a friend
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Mum jogs behind her pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, used in old-fashioned British slang.

clue.text: Newly built bistro next to lake in English city

indicators.note: something newly built has been put together afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new restaurant opens by the water in a city in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly built' is the anagram signal, reshuffling the restaurant word; 'next to' is just a link placing the lake's letter alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a large port city in south-west England.

clue.text: Provider of cakes consumed in break

indicators.note: consumed means used up and broken down, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cake seller's goods are eaten during a tea break.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker makes bread and pastries for sale.

clue.text: Make haste to prepare for some rollerblading

definitions.meaning: put wheeled boots on one's feet

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hurry up, and literally means strapping on wheeled footwear before skating.

clue.text: Refuse to accept hard defeat

indicators.note: to accept means the rubbish takes the hard letter inside it

parts.note: refuse means rubbish, trash
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone declines to take a heavy loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce an opponent is to beat them soundly.

clue.text: Care for a girl

explanation.definitionFit: Prudence means careful good judgement, and it is also a woman's given name.
